question: A 40-year-old man comes to the physician because of weight gain over the past 3 months. During this period, he has gained 10 kg (22 lb) unintentionally. He also reports decreased sexual desire, oily skin, and sleeping difficulties. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 10 years. The patient appears lethargic. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Physical examination shows central obesity, acne, and thin, easily bruisable skin with stretch marks on the abdomen. There is darkening of the mucous membranes and the skin creases. Examination of the muscles shows atrophy and weakness of proximal muscle groups. His serum glucose concentration is 240 mg/dL. Which of the following findings would most likely be present on imaging?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Elevated serum glucose concentration -> Insulin resistance -> Increased insulin production -> Hyperinsulinemia -> Increased androgen production -> Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) -> Ovarian theca cell hyperplasia -> Pituitary microadenoma -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely finding on imaging for this patient with symptoms of weight gain, decreased sexual desire, oily skin, and hyperglycemia, along with physical exam findings of central obesity, acne, thin skin, and muscle weakness, would be a pituitary microadenoma. This is supported by the reasoning chain linking elevated serum glucose concentration to insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, increased androgen production, and ultimately to the development of PCOS and ovarian theca cell hyperplasia, which can lead to a pituitary microadenoma in about 80% of cases.
analysis: The patient's presentation with symptoms of weight gain, decreased sexual desire, oily skin, hyperglycemia, central obesity, acne, thin skin, muscle weakness, and the enhanced information linking these findings to a pituitary microadenoma strongly suggests this as the most likely cause. Pituitary microadenomas can lead to hormonal imbalances that manifest in the symptoms described.
